meta.name: LeClap before / after evidence
meta.description: House template for a UI change: the defect on the merge base and the fix on the branch, played side by side and in step, between a LeClap slate and its closing card. build.py composes the comparison clip (the two panes, their labels, the baked freeze and the callouts) from global.variables and hands it over as a project_video; LeClap draws the slate, the headline, the frame highlights, the clap and the join. Every value the engine would otherwise default is pinned: an evidence video has to render the same on a re-run months later. The deliberate omissions are `look` and `grade`, because a colour grade would shift the very UI colours the video exists to prove.
meta.creativeDirection: Audience: a reviewer reading a pull request. Brand: LeClap, on its ink canvas, with the lavender to pink gradient, the Oswald display face, Rubik for copy and Roboto Mono for slate data. Hierarchy: the headline, then the one-line summary, then the BEFORE and AFTER fields. Motion: one signature move per card (tracking-in on the intro headline, rise on the outro), a hinged clapper that claps once on the cut into the comparison, and the frame highlight during the freeze. Nothing moves under text that is being read: no push, wipe or camera move, fades only between sections. Review: every label readable while on screen, both panes uncropped, the freeze long enough to read the callouts.

ticket.description: The pull or merge request, as the slate's ROLL field, e.g. PR #109.

headline.description: The change, in capitals. build.py refuses a headline wider than one line of the slate.

summary.default: Add to cart becomes a primary button that opens the cart
summary.description: The change in one line: under the intro headline and again on the outro.

beforeChip.description: What the merge base does, in a few words, beside its badge on the slate.

afterChip.description: What the branch does, in a few words, beside its badge on the slate.

outroSubtitle.default: Button contrast first, then focus in the drawer

clipSeconds.description: Length of the two runs in seconds, before any freeze. build.py cuts both captures to it and writes it, plus the hold, into the resolved template, so the cut and the render cannot disagree.

variables._note: Design tokens for the comparison clip build.py composes with ffmpeg; the slate and the outro carry the same values in their HTML layers, so change both together. Values are strings because global.variables is record(string, string | string[]). Margins and the gutter are 32 px and every vertical step sits on a 4 px grid. Colours are the LeClap dark-theme tokens (DESIGN.md): ink canvas, secondary-500 rose for BEFORE and brand-400 lavender for AFTER, a luminance-matched pair that both carry ink text at AA.
